question: Will AfD win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Persistent polls place CDU/Greens ahead of AfD in Baden-Württemberg, making AfD the unlikely largest party in seats.
Historical base-rate in BW shows AfD has never led the state; coalitions typically exclude AfD, restricting its upside.
There is a non-zero tail risk from outlier dynamics (e.g., late surges or turnout shifts), but such momentum has not been sustained in subsequent polling.
The ensemble aggregate (2%) underweights the current polling and historical context, warranting a modest upward calibration.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections largely validate that the ensemble underestimates the likelihood of an AfD-lead, driven by base-rate and polling evidence; the outlier upside is real but not sustained, supporting an upward adjustment rather than a downward correction.
justification.adjustment: Increased from 0.02 to 0.08 to align with credible polling around 19–22% for AfD but still well below the leading CDU/Greens, reflecting a small but non-negligible tail risk without implying a realistic near-term lead.

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg Landtag elections since 2011; base rate that AfD has not been the leading party in BW and is typically outpaced by CDU or Greens in this state, as reflected in contemporary polls for the 2026 election.

sources.claim: Pre-election polls in Baden-Württemberg show the CDU as the largest party (roughly 26-31%), Greens around 20-27%, and AfD trailing around about 19%, making AfD unlikely to win the most seats.
Polymarket-based forecasts indicate CDU first, Greens second, AfD third in Baden-Württemberg; AfD is not predicted to be the largest party.
The Times notes AfD national polling around the mid-20s and frames Baden-Württemberg as a contest where CDU/Greens lead rather than AfD.

Die Welt discusses YouGov polling suggesting momentum for the AfD in 2026 that includes expectations of at least one minister-president in Germany, illustrating AfD growth but not indicating BW as a likely AfD-led outcome.
As of late February 2026, polls show CDU ~29%, Greens ~23%, AfD ~20% in Baden-Württemberg.
BWTrend (October 2025): CDU 29%, AfD 21%, Greens 20% five months before the election; AfD ahead of Greens.
Infratest dimap poll (October 2025) reported CDU 29%, AfD 21%, Greens 20%.
May 2025 Infratest dimap poll cited by Statista: CDU 31%, Greens 20%, AfD 19%.
Background: In 2021 Greens were the largest party with 32.6%; AfD had 9.7%; 2026 page shows Greens 57 seats, CDU 43, AfD 17 as current seats.
Official confirmation that the 2026 Baden-Württemberg Landtag election is scheduled for 8 March 2026.
SWR confirms 8 March 2026 as the election date for Baden-Württemberg's Landtag.
Bundeswahlleiter lists the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election date for 2026 as 8 March.
Staatsanzeiger BW reports polling showing CDU ahead of Greens (INSA: CDU 31%, Greens 17%), and another poll (Infratest dimap for SWR/Stuttgarter Zeitung) showing CDU 29%, Greens 20%, AfD 22%.
FGW/ZDF-Politbarometer (Feb 26, 2026): CDU 27%, Greens 25%, AfD 19%, SPD 9%, FDP 6% with projection indicating the governing coalition would hold a majority.

causal-factors.name: Polls show CDU ahead with Greens close, AfD far behind
causal-factors.rationale: Contemporary pre-election polls place CDU around the high 20s to ~30%, Greens near mid-20s, and AfD around 19–21%, making AfD unlikely to be the largest party.

causal-factors.name: AfD vote share trailing behind CDU/Greens in most polls
causal-factors.rationale: Repeated polling consistently shows AfD behind CDU and Greens, reducing the probability of AfD obtaining the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Outlier BWTrend poll suggested AfD could overtake Greens in Oct 2025
causal-factors.rationale: An outlier indicating AfD ahead of Greens could lift the likelihood of AfD leading if replicated, though subsequent polls did not sustain this lead.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets rank AfD behind CDU and Greens
causal-factors.rationale: Market-based forecasts (e.g., Polymarket) place AfD in third behind CDU and Greens, dampening the probability of AfD being the largest.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate: AfD has never led BW in state elections
causal-factors.rationale: Long-run BW history shows AfD has not led the state, anchoring expectations toward CDU/Greens.

causal-factors.name: Potential late-campaign dynamics or turnout effects could benefit AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Late shifts or higher turnout among AfD supporters could nudge them upward, though the evidence for a sustained shift is uncertain.

causal-factors.name: Persistent polling gap: CDU/Greens ahead of AfD in Baden-Württemberg polls
causal-factors.rationale: Across polls in 2025–2026, AfD polls around 19–22% while CDU and Greens rate higher, making AfD unlikely to be the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Outlier late-2025 BWTrend scenario where AfD led Greens
causal-factors.rationale: BWTrend (Oct 2025) reported AfD ahead of Greens; if such a shift persisted, AfD could threaten the lead, but the pattern did not endure.

causal-factors.name: Regional political culture and coalition dynamics favoring CDU/Greens
causal-factors.rationale: BW’s history of CDU/Greens dominance and the likelihood of coalitions excluding AfD reduce the odds of AfD becoming the largest party.

causal-factors.name: National AfD momentum not reliably translating to Baden-Württemberg
causal-factors.rationale: National polling around the mid-20s for AfD does not consistently lift BW support above 20% in state polls.

causal-factors.name: Turnout dynamics and AfD voter mobilization potential
causal-factors.rationale: A turnout surge among AfD supporters could modestly lift their share and thus the chance of leading the state, if it materializes.

causal-factors.name: Polling lead of CDU and Greens over AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Late February 2026 polls place CDU around 27–29%, Greens around 23–25%, and AfD around 19–21%, implying AfD is unlikely to overtake the two main parties and win the most seats. (Sources: FGW/ZDF Politbarometer via turn3view0; INSA-based polls via turn1view0 and turn2view0)

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets and polls not projecting AfD as largest
causal-factors.rationale: Polymarket forecasts and other outlets generally rank AfD behind CDU/Greens for Baden-Württemberg, reducing the probability that AfD wins the most seats. (Source: turn0search0)

causal-factors.name: Seat distribution and majority dynamics constrain AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Projected compositions show AfD well behind CDU and Greens in seats (e.g., CDU ~36, Greens ~28, AfD ~26; majority threshold is 61), meaning AfD would not be the largest party and would face coalition hurdles. (Sources: turn3view0; turn0search16)

causal-factors.name: Recent campaign developments could modestly boost AfD momentum
causal-factors.rationale: AfD-related campaign developments, such as public appearances abroad by the top candidate, could provide a small, temporary momentum boost. (Source: turn0news13)

synthesis: Current credible polls and BW political history imply AfD is unlikely to win the most seats, though a small tail risk exists from late dynamics. I calibrated upward from the ensemble 2% to around 8% to reflect base-rate and poll context while keeping the probability well below a plausible leading scenario.
